VideoOut.notes: The position mapping is at VideoOut.cpp:82-89: in the bipolar setting the voltage divided by ten plus a half is multiplied by the screen size, so -5V is the left or top edge and +5V the right or bottom; in the unipolar setting 0V to 10V covers the same span. Colour is clamped between 0 and 0.999 and multiplied by 256 (lines 106-115), so voltages past the ends of the range are held at black and white rather than wrapping. The separate window is redrawn once every sampleRate/30 samples (line 152). The panel display and the pop-out window hold their own copies of the image, which is why the code keeps two 'resolution changed' flags.

ImageIn.notes: Positions are folded rather than clamped at ImageIn.cpp:73-78 through fold_into_range, so a voltage outside the chosen range reads a mirrored copy of the picture. The colour comes out as ten times the byte divided by 256 (lines 92-101), with five volts taken off again in the bipolar setting, so the top of the range is just under the nominal maximum. The load button is tested with a plain equality against 1 at line 58 rather than an edge detector, so the dialogue opens while the button is held. The file filter list is in the source at line 41.

Picks the path: Scanning runs left to right and top to bottom, Boustrophedon alternates the direction of each line, Spiral works out from the centre, and Random jumps to a new point

Note — the head moves one step per audio sample, so at a speed of 1 and a resolution of 150 the grid is covered in 22500 samples

PathGenerator.notes: The four paths are at PathGenerator.cpp:44-99. The spiral turns when its coordinate crosses the resolution minus the other coordinate, which makes a square spiral rather than a round one. The random setting compares a fresh uniform number against the speed knob each sample, so at a speed of 1 it picks a new pixel every sample. The output voltage is ten times the position over the resolution, with five taken off in the bipolar setting (lines 101-105), so the head never quite reaches the top of the range.

CoordinateFolder.notes: The square fold at CoordinateFolder.cpp:63-65 takes each coordinate modulo ten over the amount, and the radial fold at lines 67-71 takes the angle modulo two pi over the amount and rebuilds the point at the same distance from the origin. The modulation at line 48 is a crossfade between the knob and the jack voltage plus one, not a scaled addition, so a fully turned modulation knob discards the amount knob entirely. The result is passed through std::abs, so a negative amount gives the same fold as its positive.

AffineTransform.notes: Each modulation trimmer is a crossfade, not an attenuator: lerp_at at AffineTransform.cpp:161 mixes the knob against the jack voltage, so a trimmer at the far right discards its knob altogether. The knob values are multiplied by five before the crossfade and the result divided by five afterwards for scale, skew and rotation, which is why 5V at a jack means a factor of one, or a whole turn for rotation. The skew at lines 141-142 updates x first and then uses the new x when working out y, so the vertical skew compounds with the horizontal one. The three output jacks run X, Y and then the two-channel one across the panel, which is not their index order: the two-channel output is index 0 and sits on the right.

PreciseDelay.notes: The delay lines are 32 samples deep (PreciseDelay.cpp:34-39) and all sixteen channels are copied every sample whether or not the input carries them, with the output channel count taken from the input at lines 102-107. No family is given to any of these jacks: they carry whatever is patched into them, so no colour would be true of them. The read index is (write pointer + 33 - delay) modulo 32, so a setting of 1 is a one-sample delay.
